verdict.rationale: The SDK ships its own schema validation: structured outputs return validated JSON matching a defined schema and re-prompt the agent on mismatch, so the agent corrects its own output errors. It also exposes typed APIs (TypeScript `Options`, Python `ClaudeAgentOptions`). However, that validation runs at runtime rather than build time, and nothing documents strict compile-time typing that catches agent mistakes. missing for 10: documented build-time/compile-time type checking of agent outputs or tool inputs, evidence of strict typed tool schemas, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can rely on strict typing and schema validation so a coding agent catches its own mistakes at build time

citations.quote: the SDK validates the output against it, re-prompting on mismatch.
you still get validated JSON matching your schema at the end.
Every `query()` call accepts an options object: `Options` in TypeScript, `ClaudeAgentOptions` in Python.
